headline: Rocket Lab posts a record quarter, beats its own guidance
summary_short: Rocket Lab's Q1 2026 revenue rose 63.5% y/y (11.5% q/q) to a record $200.3M, with GAAP gross margin expanding to 38.2% and net loss narrowing to $45.0M (-$0.07/share diluted) from $60.6M a year earlier, as backlog grew to $2.2B.
summary_long: Revenue grew 63.5% y/y (11.5% q/q) to a record $200.3M across launch and space systems, with GAAP gross margin expanding to 38.2% from 28.8% and non-GAAP gross margin to 43.0% from 33.4%. Operating loss narrowed to $56.0M and net loss to $45.0M (-$0.07 diluted GAAP EPS) from $60.6M a year earlier. The company signed 31 new Electron/HASTE contracts plus five dedicated Neutron launches, closed the Mynaric acquisition, and agreed to acquire Motiv Space Systems, lifting backlog to $2.2B (+20.2% q/q). Cash and equivalents rose to $1,205.5M after a $450M ATM equity raise; convertible notes fell to $36.9M. Rocket Lab guided Q2 2026 revenue to $225M-$240M, GAAP gross margin to 33%-35%, and Adjusted EBITDA loss of $20M-$26M.

drivers.explanation: Record quarter driven by broad execution across launch and space systems programs; space systems revenue $136.7M and launch revenue $63.7M, both up sharply y/y.
GAAP gross margin rose to 38.2% from 28.8% y/y; the release attributes margin strength to program execution across launch and space systems, without a single quantified driver.
Loss narrowed as gross-profit growth outpaced a rise in operating expenses (R&D and SG&A both up) tied to continued Neutron development and headcount/integration costs.
Narrower operating loss plus higher net interest income (from a larger cash balance) more than offset the year's other expense items.
Follows the smaller net loss, partly offset by a higher weighted-average diluted share count (605.4M vs 505.6M y/y).
Not explained in the release at the shard's Yahoo-sourced EBITDA definition; the company's own Adjusted EBITDA of -$11.75M reflects add-backs for stock-based compensation, D&A, and transaction costs.
Cash rose to $1,205.5M largely on $450.3M of proceeds from at-the-market equity offerings during the quarter.
Not explained in the release; the balance sheet shows the convertible senior notes balance falling from $152.4M (Q4 2025) to $36.9M.
Equity growth reflects the year's ATM equity raises and additional paid-in capital growth, partly offset by the accumulated deficit.
Company says it surpassed all of its own Q1 guidance metrics (revenue, margin, Adjusted EBITDA); signed a record number of new launch contracts and guided another record-revenue quarter for Q2 2026.
